title: The Fox and the North Wind
logline: When the north wind blows for three nights, a white fox comes to the door and must be given a gift. This time, Nell has to answer.
style: Mike Mignola style adapted for children ages 9-11: heavy black inks, thick confident brushstrokes, flat shadows with no gradients or soft shading, warm cream and sepia palette with deep Arctic blue night, red-painted Swedish wood. Cozy but atmospheric, never scary. Hand-inked animated film look, 2D, painterly flat colour, cinematic 16:9 composition. No text, no letters, no typography, no captions, no watermark. No fire or flames unless the description explicitly asks for them.
motionStyle: Cut-paper 2.5D animation: flat illustrated layers moving in depth, gentle parallax, slow camera, no morphing, no text appearing.

narrator.notes: Warm, unhurried storyteller reading a bedtime story to a 10-year-old. Gentle pauses at commas. Never theatrical.

farmor.notes: An old Swedish grandmother speaking English carefully, with small pauses, the way people do when translating in their head. Quiet, warm, a little solemn.

nell.notes: A curious, brave 10-year-old girl. Natural and soft, a little breathless when nervous.

shots.keyframe: Wide establishing shot of the village of Jokkmokk under a deep blue Arctic sky at midday twilight; Farmor's small red house at the edge of the frozen lake, pine forest layered behind.
shots.motion: Very slow push in through the layers of pines.

lines.text: Above the Arctic Circle, in the north of Sweden, the winter sun rises at ten and sets at one. The rest of the day is deep blue, turning to black.

shots.keyframe: Nell walks through deep snow towards the red house, pulling a small suitcase; one window glows warm yellow.
shots.motion: Nell trudges forward, breath clouding.

lines.text: This is where Nell spent Christmas when she was ten, in her grandmother's small red house at the edge of a frozen lake.

shots.keyframe: Inside by the wood stove: Farmor, white braid down her back, pulls two wooden chairs to the fire; Måns sleeps in his basket; Nell wrapped in a blanket.
shots.motion: Farmor sets the chairs down and sits; firelight flickers.

lines.text: Farmor Astrid was small and quiet, with a white braid down her back.
There is a story I need to tell you.

shots.keyframe: Flashback in cut-paper silhouettes and blue tones: a sailor lost in a snowy forest follows a small floating light between the trees; at his own door the light becomes a small white fox.
shots.motion: The light drifts ahead; the sailor follows; the light settles into the shape of a fox.

lines.text: Long ago, a sailor in our family was lost in the winter forest. A light led him home, and at his door, the light became a small white fox with amber eyes.

shots.keyframe: Flashback montage on the same doorstep across generations: a coin, a piece of bread, a feather left in the snow; fox tracks leading to each.
shots.motion: Each gift appears in turn on the step.

lines.text: When the north wind blows for three nights, the fox comes to the door. And a gift must be given. Honestly.

shots.keyframe: Close two-shot of Nell and Farmor lit by the fire.
shots.motion: Nell leans in; Farmor looks into the flames.

lines.text: And if you don't?
Then the fox takes something else.

shots.keyframe: Night, Nell's small bedroom; snow streams sideways past the window; Nell gets out of bed.
shots.motion: The wind shakes the window; Nell crosses to it.

lines.text: That night, the wind came out of the north, humming one long, low note around the corners of the house.

shots.keyframe: The moonlit yard seen from the window: small fresh fox tracks lead through bright snow right up to the front door.
shots.motion: Slow tilt down along the tracks to the door.

lines.text: In the snow by the front door, small tracks. Fox tracks. Fresh.

shots.keyframe: Morning blue light; Farmor at the kitchen window holding a cup of coffee, the wind still bending the pines outside.
shots.motion: Farmor sips, watching.

lines.text: Two nights. One more, and the fox will come.

shots.keyframe: Kitchen table: Farmor blows dust off a very small old wooden box with a lid that does not quite fit; she opens it; it is empty.
shots.motion: Dust lifts in the light; the lid opens.
shots.sfx: a soft breath, a wooden creak

lines.text: Farmor brought out the old offering box. It was empty.

shots.keyframe: Flashback in blue tones: young Astrid holds out a gold necklace on the doorstep; the white fox looks at it, then at her, and turns away. Then: an empty ring dish on a dresser.
shots.motion: The fox turns and leaves; cut to the empty dish.

lines.text: Once, I gave a gold necklace. The fox looked at it, and left. The next morning, my father's silver ring was gone.

shots.keyframe: Nell and Farmor baking bread together, flour on the table, the wind rattling the windows.
shots.motion: Farmor stops kneading and looks at Nell.

lines.text: What did the sailor do that worked?
He was frightened, and alone in the trees. So he sang.

shots.keyframe: Nell lies awake in bed in the dark, eyes open, moonlight across the quilt.
shots.motion: Slow push in on Nell's face.

lines.text: By morning, Nell knew what she would give.

shots.keyframe: The third night by the front door: Nell in boots, coat and knitted hat; Farmor places the small wooden box in her hands.
shots.motion: Farmor nods once.

lines.text: I need to do this on my own.

shots.keyframe: The doorstep in bright moonlight; the small white fox steps out of the pines and sits in the snow a metre from Nell.
shots.motion: The fox emerges and sits very still.

lines.text: The fox was smaller than she had expected. White as the snow. Eyes of amber.

shots.keyframe: Nell kneels, sets the wooden box on the step and sings; the wind drops, snowflakes slow, the pines stand still.
shots.motion: Snow slows almost to a stop around them.

lines.text: Vem kan segla förutan vind, vem kan ro utan åror.

shots.keyframe: The fox walks to the box, looks up at Nell, bows its head once, then turns and disappears into the trees.
shots.motion: The bow, slow and deliberate; the fox trots away.

lines.text: The fox bowed its head, once, like someone accepting a gift, and was gone.

shots.keyframe: By the fire: Farmor sees the empty box in Nell's hands and her eyes fill with tears.
shots.motion: Farmor puts a hand over her mouth, then an arm around Nell.

lines.text: You sang.
Mama's lullaby.
My mother's song.

shots.keyframe: Morning: Farmor writes the verses in careful spidery handwriting, folds the paper and places it inside the small box.
shots.motion: She closes the lid gently.

lines.text: For the next one. In case they don't remember the words.

shots.keyframe: The still snowy forest at dawn; far off, the small white fox trots home between the pines.
shots.motion: The fox grows smaller in the distance.

lines.text: Somewhere far off, a small white fox carried something home that only it could hear.
